episodes.189275: Severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front when then ran into the sea breeze. The environment was quite unstable and the shear was fairly strong.
episodes.189624: Late evening thunderstorms moved through the southeastern portions of Eastern NC. One such storm produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.189788: A cold front draped across central North Carolina served as a focus for thunderstorm redevelopment during the afternoon as the cold front shifted slowly south. Supercells developed across the southern Piedmont, Sandhills, and southern Coastal Plain Counties. The severe storms went on to produce prolific hail ranging from ping pong to just over hen egg size across southern portions of central North Carolina. One supercell thunderstorm went on to produce 3-4 inch hail in nearby Robeson County.
episodes.190164: Late afternoon and early evening isolated strong to severe storms produced wind damage across NE FL south of the I-10 corridor and near the local Atlantic coast.
episodes.190167: Late afternoon and early evening isolated strong to severe storms produced wind damage across NE FL south of the I-10 corridor and near the local Atlantic coast.
episodes.190168: Late afternoon and early evening isolated strong to severe storms produced wind damage across NE FL south of the I-10 corridor and near the local Atlantic coast.
episodes.190612: A strong trough over northeastern Mexico pushed a cold front down into South Texas late in the evening of the 20th into the early morning hours of the 21st, setting up a favorable environment for supercells. A few supercells developed over the Brush Country and Victoria Crossroads. Large hail was reported in Goliad and Duval Counties.
episodes.190660: A cold front positioned near the southeast South Carolina coast along with modest instability led to thunderstorms capable of producing severe/damaging winds gusts.
episodes.190702: A stalled frontal boundary draped across the deep south from Texas to Louisiana began to move southward as a cold front. This happened in response to an upper system moving through the Mississippi Valley on April 20th. Although instability was quite weak, there was enough buoyancy in place in combination with lift provided by the cold front to support a few severe thunderstorms over local coastal waters.
episodes.191146: An upper level shortwave trough moved over Texas and generated thunderstorms along a surface trough. Some of these storms produced large hail.
